newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia noon rubber steady, INRO news no impact.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia noon rubber steady, INRO news no impact.

text.p: Malaysian rubber prices held steady at noon on Friday with gains in Tokyo and scattered local dealers' covering seen, dealers said.

They said overnight news that the International Natural Rubber Organisation (INRO) is set to resume rubber market intervention to stabilise prices following the launch of a new global accord has no immediate impact.

One trader at a broking firm said: "The INRO news has no immediate impact but if prices continue to fall to near his (INRO buffer stock manager) "may-buy" or "must-buy" level, then we will see what happen."
INRO's five-day moving average price was 212.96 Malaysian/Singapore cents a kg on June 12 against 213.80 on June 11. INRO's "may buy" level is 176 cents and "must buy" level is 165.
Generally, the market was inactive this morning with lack of strong interest from the Far East affecting sentiment.
"The Europeans have more or less covered their positions for the summer break and are staying away," a dealer said, adding that latex demand was only seen from local manufacturers.
